corrections.original_claim: [RECOMMENDATION] add a `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production" && <style ...>` block in app/layout.tsx's <head>.
corrections.truth: This gate is wrong for this codebase's actual deployment. Netlify sets NODE_ENV=production on deploy previews and branch deploys too, so the marker would be INVISIBLE on exactly the preview URLs the owner looks at — the failure the whole task exists to fix. The repo already knows this and says so in three places: lib/env.ts:242-251 ('Netlify sets CONTEXT to production / deploy-preview / branch-deploy, and combined with NODE_ENV this narrows to the one context...'), lib/ratelimit.ts:264-266 ('CONTEXT alone is Netlify-set on deploy previews/branch deploys too, so pairing it with NODE_ENV is the defense-in-depth line'), lib/health.ts:88-92. The correct predicate, matching the estate's own idiom, is `!(process.env.CONTEXT === "production" && process.env.NODE_ENV === "production")`. It is safe in app/layout.tsx specifically because that file is a server component; the same expression in a client component would read CONTEXT as undefined and mark everywhere.

The logic works; nothing ever calls it. net_picture:
The recon's factual core holds up under adversarial re-checking. I independently reproduced all 19 of its data and code claims that I marked CONFIRMED, including every live-database number to the digit (20 visible salons, 20/20 Unsplash covers, 11 distinct, 13 sharing, the exact 4x/4x/3x/2x duplicate groups and salon names, 166/174 gallery URLs across 37 distinct, is_test false on all 28 rows, discovery_items at 136 Pexels of 1000 sampled) and every one of roughly 60 cited file:line pairs I opened. Two of its claims turn out stronger than stated: salon_photos is 0 rows LIVE, not just in the ten-day-old snapshot, and the admin seeder really is the only in-repo writer of salons.cover_photo_url (the one other cover_photo_url write, app/api/staff/[id]/slug/route.ts:51, targets staff_members).

Six things are wrong or overstated. The two that change what you should do:

First, "no isStock helper exists" is now false. lib/stock-image.ts exists, exporting STOCK_IMAGE_HOSTS, isStockImageUrl() and stockImageProvider(). It is untracked (created today) and has ZERO importers. Its header names three consumers: StockPhotoMarker, which exists nowhere on disk; scripts/check-invariants.mjs, which does not import it; and a hook. So the helper is itself the repo's signature failure, a control that looks wired and does nothing.

Second, and more consequential, the enforcement layer is not absent, it is half-wired. ~/.claude/hooks/stock-photo-gate.py implements a PreToolUse blocker and a Stop blocker in one file, and ~/.claude/settings.json registers it on Stop ONLY (hooks/Stop[22]/hooks[2]). I self-tested the file: its PreToolUse branch correctly denies an unsplash URL baked into app/[locale]/booking/lookup/page.tsx and correctly passes a mockup path. The logic is right; nothing calls it. Registering it on a PreToolUse Write|Edit|MultiEdit matcher is a one-line change and is the highest-value action here, higher than the CSS marker.

Third, the recommended `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"` gate is wrong for this deployment. Netlify sets NODE_ENV=production on deploy previews and branch deploys, so the marker would be invisible on precisely the preview URLs the owner inspects. The codebase documents this in three places (lib/env.ts:242-251, lib/ratelimit.ts:264-266, lib/health.ts:88-92) and uses `CONTEXT === "production" && NODE_ENV === "production"` as its real-prod test. Use the negation of that. It is safe in app/layout.tsx because that file is a server component.

The remaining corrections are smaller. The NODE_ENV survey is wrong (72 hits, 14 outside /dev/, not 30). The Unsplash literal denominator is 48 occurrences across 47 lines, not 46, though the 28-dead subset is exactly right and its dead-code proof is sound. Three mockups reference the missing p01-p12.jpg, not four (the fourth reference is _BASE.md itself). check-invariants' Invariant E is not aging scaffolding; commit 87128e9be landed it today, so "still true ten days later" misreads same-day work as neglect. app/layout.tsx is not the only <html> in the app (app/global-error.tsx:16 has its own, with no <head>), though the injection-point conclusion survives.

One surface the recon never covered: staff_members.avatar_url is 65/70 Unsplash live. That reinforces the headline and argues specifically for the URL-keyed CSS approach over any flag scoped to the salons table, which would miss staff imagery entirely. Two free cleanups fall out of the verification: picsum can be dropped from next.config.mjs:106,110 and the netlify.toml CSP because the PROOF_SALON_ITEMS it was added for are already removed (app/[locale]/inspo/page.tsx:32) and no live row uses it, and netlify.toml:52 is Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only, so it enforces nothing regardless.
